findings: The photon energy is the remainder of the jet share, not a radiation calculation: any charged energy the nozzle does not direct (plasma heat, undirected debris, the driver energy) is booked as X-rays.
Neutron heating is the neutron energy times the photon sky fraction: neutrons were given the photon geometry and full absorption.
The sky fraction is an axisymmetric (x, rho) screen: the eight cage longerons count as a solid surface of revolution, and parts that are not coils, shield or cage are missing.
Every intercepted photon deposits all its energy where it lands (no transmission, scattering or depth).

LOW.note: burn held at the D-3He optimum in hot-ion mode (electrons at half the ion temperature): a lower bound, not a demonstrated burn

NOMINAL.note: equilibrated thermal burn held at the D-3He optimum

CONSERVATIVE.note: self-consistent burn of the implied target to the demonstrator yield: the fusion protons heat the electrons, which radiate

codes.Geant4: Apache-2.0-like Geant4 licence, free; C++ toolkit, needs a GDML export of the meshes and a physics list (Livermore/Penelope EM); about a day of setup, minutes of CPU at 1e6 photons for this scene
codes.OpenMC: MIT, free; photon transport since 0.12 with CAD via DAGMC; needs nuclear and photon data libraries (several GB); best for the neutron channel
codes.xraylib: BSD; photoelectric/Compton/pair cross sections; install was not permitted in this session
codes.run: NONE: neither is installed; the brackets are the result

cluster.note: First hit from engine N1 (the four engines are symmetric); behind_first: the next owner a ray meets after leaving its first one (what transmitted photons and neutrons can reach). Hull and habitat beyond the radiator roots are not in the scene.

thermal.note: Capacity: radiators.effective_area (both faces, view factor 0.9) at 1800 K and emissivity 0.9, the whole hot radiator, with nothing reserved for the ship's other hot loads (a favourable assumption). The WARM and LOW sections carry the ship's own loads and cannot take engine heat at these powers. Storage is not closure (T3).

T1.verdict: The heat leaves with the hydrogen, but at a thermal exhaust speed about 1/3000 of the fusion exhaust: carrying the absorbed heat needs a hydrogen flow millions of times the engine propellant flow, which the mission mass cannot pay. At a hydrogen flow equal to the engine flow it recovers kilowatts. Radiator demand is unchanged.

T2.verdict: Conversion makes driver power but rejects the rest at a lower temperature: more radiator area, not less.

T3.note: ESTIMATE: the engine mass estimate (vertex_engine.mass_estimate), cp 500 J/(kg K), 1000 K swing. Buffering delays the heat; it never removes it.

gap.text: The photons may be at most this share of the fusion yield for four engines to fit the radiators, even with neutrons and charged heat at zero and the most favourable transport bracket.

scan_min.text: The lowest photon share in the R2-A plasma scan (Te/Ti down to 0.1, which no dense burn holds) still exceeds the requirement.

alternatives.name: Hotter ions, cooler electrons (hot-ion mode)
alternatives.physics: Bremsstrahlung falls with Te; D-He3 at Ti 110 keV with Te/Ti 0.5 gives the LOW case. Electron-ion equilibration in a dense burn makes Te/Ti < 1 hard to hold (R2-B runs to Te = Ti).

alternatives.name: Target composition (pure fuel, D-rich mix)
alternatives.physics: The fuel is already Z_eff-minimal; any high-Z tamper raises bremsstrahlung as Z^2; a D-rich mix adds D-D neutrons and tritium (sensitivity rows).

alternatives.name: Optically thick target (photon trapping)
alternatives.physics: Hard bremsstrahlung (30-1000 keV) is not reabsorbed: free-free absorption is negligible and hot-electron Compton gives energy to photons. Trapping needs high-Z (raising emission) or rhoR far beyond the 97 g/cm2 the yield already implies.

alternatives.name: Pusher standoff (open nozzle, only a distant shadow shield)
alternatives.physics: A shield at distance D covering a disc of radius R takes (1-cos atan(R/D))/2 of the sky. The magnetic nozzle at that distance cannot capture the charged products: thrust is then the shield's own ablation and momentum (pulse unit), a different engine.
alternatives.verdict: CLOSES THERMALLY ONLY AS A DIFFERENT ENGINE

alternatives.name: Magnetic redirection or mirrors for X-rays
alternatives.physics: Photons carry no charge; grazing-incidence optics reflect keV X-rays below about 1 degree and nothing above about 100 keV.

alternatives.name: Direct X-ray conversion (photoelectric / thermionic blanket)
alternatives.physics: Converts part of the absorbed heat to electricity but rejects the rest at a lower temperature (T-REG T2): more radiator, not less, unless the electricity is exported (it has nowhere to go but the driver).

speculative.quantity: photon share of the fusion yield

speculative.machinery: a burn regime below the bremsstrahlung floor: Te far below Ti with no equilibration, which no known plasma state holds
